issues.description: The problem statement and template define/expect a method named addParent(Person person, Person parent) in PersonService, and tests and PersonResource invoke personService.addParent(...). In the solution implementation the corresponding method is named registerParent(Person person, Person parent) (and no addParent implementation is present). This name/signature mismatch between solution, template, tests, and REST resource is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students comparing template/tests with the provided solution and can cause compilation errors in the solution codebase.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's registerParent(Person, Person) method to addParent(Person, Person) (or add a delegating addParent method that calls registerParent) so that method names and signatures are consistent between the problem statement, template, tests, and REST resource. Ensure the solution compiles and tests invoke the same service method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a service method named addParent(Person, Person) (students are instructed to implement addParent and PersonResource invokes personService.addParent). In the solution implementation the corresponding service method is named registerParent(Person, Person). This mismatch (addParent vs. registerParent) creates a clear identifier naming inconsistency across artifacts and will confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's registerParent(Person, Person) to addParent(Person, Person) (or add an addParent wrapper that delegates to registerParent) so that the problem statement, template, tests, PersonResource, and service implementation all refer to the same identifier.
